scheme_name: Additional Pension to 100% Disabled Ex-Serviceman having No Child
description:
The scheme titled "Additional Pension to 100% Disabled Ex-Servicemen having No Child" was launched by the Government of India to provide financial assistance to a specific group of individuals who have served in the armed forces and have been rendered completely disabled due to their service. 

The scheme was initiated on 1st April 2019. 

It aims to support ex-servicemen who are 100% disabled and do not have any children. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to ensure that these individuals receive additional financial support to help them manage their living expenses. 

The government recognizes the sacrifices made by ex-servicemen and aims to provide them with a dignified life post-service. 

The additional pension is intended to supplement the existing pension that these individuals receive from the government. 

The additional pension amount is set at ₹15,000 per month. 

This amount is provided on top of the regular pension that the ex-serviceman is already receiving. 

The scheme is particularly beneficial for those who do not have any children to support them in their old age. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specific and stringent. 

Only ex-servicemen who have been declared 100% disabled due to service-related injuries or ailments are eligible. 

Furthermore, applicants must not have any children, biological or adopted. 

There are no specific age limits mentioned in the eligibility criteria. 

However, the applicant must be a retired personnel from the Indian Armed Forces, which includes the Army, Navy, and Air Force. 

The application process for this scheme is straightforward but requires specific documentation. 

Interested ex-servicemen must fill out the prescribed application form available at the nearest Zila Sainik Board or online through the official government portal. 

The application form must be accompanied by a copy of the disability certificate issued by the competent authority. 

Additionally, a copy of the pension payment order is required to verify the existing pension amount. 

Ex-servicemen must also provide proof of not having any children, which could include a self-declaration affidavit. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the concerned authorities at the Zila Sainik Board. 

The processing time for the application is typically around 30 days from the date of submission. 

If approved, the additional pension will be disbursed along with the regular pension. 

The disbursement of the additional pension occurs on a monthly basis. 

The funds are credited directly to the bank account of the ex-serviceman. 

This ensures that the financial assistance is received in a timely manner without any delays. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. 

The Zila Sainik Boards across various states are responsible for the ground-level implementation and monitoring of the scheme. 

Ex-servicemen can contact the Zila Sainik Board in their respective districts for any queries related to the scheme. 

The contact details for the Zila Sainik Boards can be found on the official website of the Ministry of Defence. 

This scheme is part of a broader initiative by the government to enhance the welfare of ex-servicemen and their families. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹500 crores for the welfare of ex-servicemen in the financial year 2022-2023. 

This allocation includes various schemes aimed at providing financial assistance, healthcare, and rehabilitation services to ex-servicemen. 

The additional pension scheme specifically addresses the needs of those who have been severely affected by their service. 

It recognizes the unique challenges faced by 100% disabled ex-servicemen who may not have familial support. 

The scheme is also aligned with the government's commitment to ensuring social security for vulnerable populations. 

As of October 2023, it is estimated that around 10,000 ex-servicemen are eligible for this additional pension across the country. 

The government aims to increase awareness about the scheme to ensure that all eligible individuals can benefit from it. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted through various media channels to reach out to ex-servicemen. 

The scheme not only provides financial support but also aims to enhance the dignity and respect for ex-servicemen in society. 

The additional pension can significantly improve the quality of life for these individuals. 

It allows them to afford better healthcare services and meet their daily living expenses. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have expressed gratitude for the financial assistance. 

The government continues to monitor the implementation of the scheme to ensure that it meets its objectives. 

Regular audits and evaluations are conducted to assess the impact of the scheme on the lives of ex-servicemen. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare measures that include housing schemes, employment opportunities, and health care services for ex-servicemen. 

The government remains committed to the welfare of ex-servicemen and their families. 

This commitment is reflected in the continuous improvement and expansion of welfare schemes. 

The Additional Pension to 100% Disabled Ex-Servicemen having No Child is a crucial step in recognizing the sacrifices made by these brave individuals. 

It is a testament to the government's dedication to providing support to those who have served the nation. 

The scheme not only addresses financial needs but also aims to foster a sense of community and belonging among ex-servicemen. 

Overall, the scheme plays a vital role in ensuring that 100% disabled ex-servicemen without children can live with dignity and respect. 

The government encourages all eligible individuals to take advantage of this scheme and apply for the additional pension. 

This initiative is a significant part of India's efforts to honor and support its veterans. 

The Additional Pension to 100% Disabled Ex-Servicemen having No Child is a crucial welfare measure that reflects the nation's gratitude towards its armed forces.
